title: Existence of list-decodable codes
statement:
Let $\alpha$ be a finite field, and fix natural numbers $n$, $L$, $M$ and a real number $p$ with $0 \le p \le 1$, $1 \le L$, $L < M$, and $M \le \abs{\alpha}^n$. Suppose $V$ is a natural number bounding the volume of every Hamming ball of radius $\lfloor pn\rfloor$, in the sense that each such ball around an arbitrary word $y \in \alpha^n$ contains at most $V$ codewords, and suppose that
\[
\abs{\alpha}^n \cdot \binom{V}{L+1} \cdot \binom{\abs{\alpha}^n - (L+1)}{\,M-(L+1)\,} \;<\; \binom{\abs{\alpha}^n}{M}.
\]
Then there exists a code $C$ of length $n$ over $\alpha$ consisting of exactly $M$ codewords that is $(p,L)$-list-decodable.
hypotheses_covered: finite field alphabet with q = |α| symbols
every Hamming ball of radius ⌊pn⌋ contains at most V codewords
the counting inequality |α|^n·C(V,L+1)·C(|α|^n−(L+1), M−(L+1)) < C(|α|^n, M)
replaced:
If the ball volume $V$ and code size $M$ satisfy the counting inequality
\[
|\alpha|^n\cdot\tbinom{V}{L+1}\cdot\tbinom{|\alpha|^n-(L+1)}{M-(L+1)}
\;<\;
\tbinom{|\alpha|^n}{M},
\]
then there exists a code $C$ of size $M$ that is $(p,L)$-list-decodable.
